text:
Priya (Support): Hey team — customer (Raj) reporting intermittent 502/504s when calling /v1/generate over the last 6 hours. They see a spike of errors correlated with token refresh events. Can someone look?

Raj (Customer): Yep, thanks. We started seeing ~0.6% 5xx rate around 10:13 UTC. Our SDK does token rotation every 15m. Attached snippet from our logs: 

```
2026-02-18T10:12:59Z INFO auth Refreshing token
2026-02-18T10:13:02Z WARN request id=abc123 status=502 message="connection reset by peer"
2026-02-18T10:13:02Z INFO retry attempt=1
2026-02-18T10:13:05Z WARN request id=abc124 status=504 message="upstream timeout"
```

Raj (Customer): We see the requests that happen <200ms after a token refresh are the ones failing. If we wait >500ms after refresh, things look fine.

Priya (Support): Interesting — likely interplay between auth handoff and connection reuse/keepalive on the edge. @Adrian can infra confirm any recent proxy changes?

Adrian (SRE): Looking. No config knobs changed in the last 24h on the public edge. I'm pulling proxy logs for the request ids Raj pasted. Quick question: is the SDK reusing HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections or HTTP/2?

Raj (Customer): Our SDK uses HTTP/1.1 keep-alive by default, reuses connections in a pool of 4. We do a header swap: Authorization: Bearer <new-token> on existing connection (no new TCP).

Sylvia (SDK): ah. that pattern is fragile if the upstream has connection-level auth expectations. We should be swapping connection or using per-request auth on a new conn. Can you paste the exact curl you use?

Raj (Customer): here's a minimal repro we ran locally: 

```
# simulate token rotation + immediate request
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD" --keepalive-time 60 https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# rotate token client-side
# immediately send
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer NEW" --keepalive-time 60 https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

Raj (Customer): The second curl sometimes returns: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway, then a stream reset.

ingress-proxy-bot: Found error pattern in proxy logs similar to Raj's ids — "upstream reset while processing request". Counting ~43 resets in last 6h from that customer IP.

Adrian (SRE): Proxy log sample: 

```
[edge-proxy] 2026-02-18T10:13:02Z conn=10.1.7.92 stream=42 upstream_error="RST_STREAM" code=2 auth_state="auth-header-changed"
```

Adrian (SRE): "auth-header-changed" tag suggests we detect header change on an existing connection and we tear down streams to avoid auth confusion. That's intentional but maybe too aggressive when swaps happen quickly.

Sylvia (SDK): We ship an SDK workaround: rotate tokens but force new connection for the first request after a refresh (set Connection: close or create new pool entry). That will avoid relying on edge behavior. We can push guidance today.

Priya (Support): For short-term mitigation — ask customer to add 500ms delay after refresh or disable connection reuse for the immediate request. Longer term we should relax edge behavior or add a header-level auth patch.

Raj (Customer): We can add a 200ms delay as a temporary workaround but it's a bit ugly. Would prefer platform change. Also seeing billing spikes: the SDK retried automatically and doubled token counts — weird billing increase for token units. Any ideas?

Adrian (SRE): Retries are expected, but saw a burst of immediate retries without exponential backoff in their client: it retries up to 3x quickly, hitting gateway and generating extra token consumption. We can add a server-side soft throttle flag to signal clients to slow down.

Priya (Support): Action plan proposed: 
- short-term: ask Raj to disable connection reuse for immediate post-refresh requests or add 300ms wait (customer accepts 200-300ms).
- SDK: Sylvia to publish workaround snippet and patch notes with code sample.
- Infra: Adrian to evaluate changing proxy behavior to not reset streams on auth header swap for 15s window as a config toggle.
- Billing: I'll open a support billing adjustment review for the retry-induced spike.

Sylvia (SDK): I'll draft the exact snippet now. Quick workaround (JS): 

```
// force new connection for post-refresh request
const opts = { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }, agent: new https.Agent({ keepAlive: false }) }
fetch(url, opts)
```

Sylvia (SDK): Publishing doc in ~30m to our SDK docs and pinging Raj.

deploy-bot: Completed canary deploy of edge-proxy v2.3.1 at 10:30 UTC (no config changes).

Adrian (SRE): I tested toggling the "auth-header-change" aggressiveness in staging. If we change behavior to allow header swaps for 10s after authentication detection, we avoid these resets for many client patterns. However that increases risk of auth replay if tokens are misapplied. Need a safety rollout and limit to 'trusted tiers' first.

Priya (Support): Can you estimate risk/rollout time? Customer is asking for timeline.

Adrian (SRE): Risk assessment: low-medium. Rollout plan: feature flag -> canary 5% -> monitor 2h -> 25% -> monitor -> full. Estimates: 6-8h to get to safe 25% canary. Requires approval from Sec/PM.

Raj (Customer): If you can do a 5% canary quickly that'd be great. Our prod traffic is a small % and a canary would likely help. Meanwhile we'll implement the SDK workaround.

Priya (Support): Great. I'll coordinate approvals and ask Billing to hold off charging for the retry spike while we investigate. 

Adrian (SRE): Kicking off feature-flag PR for the edge: https://git.internal/edge/merge/PR-892 (summary: relax stream reset on auth header change for short window behind FF). Pinged @sylvia for SDK note alignment.

Sylvia (SDK): Posted SDK advisory: "If you rotate bearer tokens in-client, force a new connection for the first request after refresh or add a small delay." Link: https://docs.internal/sdk/rotate-token. Will include code snippets for Python/JS/Go.

Priya (Support): Update for Raj: we have three concurrent mitigations — (1) customer implements SDK workaround, (2) infra canary to relax reset behavior, (3) billing hold request submitted. I'll circle back with timeline in 30m. :thumbsup: 

Raj (Customer): Implemented the keepalive:false workaround and ran load test — 0.02% 5xx over 30m vs 0.6% before. Looks good. Thanks.

Adrian (SRE): Canary started at 11:05 UTC to 5% traffic. Initial telemetry: errors from this customer dropped to baseline within seconds. Monitoring group will observe for 1h.

ingress-proxy-bot: Canary metrics: error-rate for the canary cohort: down 75% for this customer; no uptick in auth anomalies global.

Priya (Support): Awesome. Raj — can we keep the SDK workaround for 24-48h while canary ramps? We'll follow up with a permanent fix/SDK release next week.

Raj (Customer): OK, will keep it. Appreciate quick turnaround. Also, please let Billing know about the temporary spike credit.

Priya (Support): Billing ticket opened #BILL-1947 for review. Adding follow-ups: infra postmortem to eng/incident channel, SDK advisory published.

Sylvia (SDK): I'll cut an SDK patch to add an optional client flag `forceNewConnAfterRefresh` and ship in patch release tomorrow.

Adrian (SRE): Will monitor canary and if stable move to 25% at 12:30 UTC.

Priya (Support): Closing loop for now — marking thread resolved for customer communication. Will post postmortem draft after canary finishes. :white_check_mark:

Raj (Customer): Thanks everyone. Very responsive.

Priya (Support): (closing note) follow-ups: ENG-FF-892, SDK-PR-444, BILL-1947. We'll update once the canary completes.
